turns.t: Sorry we're late. The bus took forever, and then I forgot my backpack at the bus stop, so we had to go back.
It's my fault, Doctor, I was still looking for the insurance card.
Not a problem at all, you're here now. Hi there, buddy. So this is your asthma check-up. Tell me how you've been breathing lately.
Um, okay, I guess. Sometimes my chest feels kinda squeezy when I run around at recess.
Squeezy, I like that description. Is it like someone's hugging your chest too tight?
Yeah, like that. And then I have to stop and sit down for a while.
That's helpful. How long does the squeezy feeling last when you sit down?
Not long. Like, a few minutes? Then it goes away.
Okay. And what about at night? Do you ever cough when you're in bed?
Sometimes I cough at night and it wakes me up. Only a little, though.
It's more than a little, honey. I hear him coughing through the wall at least three nights a week, and some nights it goes on for a long time.
How long has the night cough been happening?
About one month, since the weather turned cold.
[from the hallway] He was wheezing a lot at the game on Saturday!
Sorry, I didn't catch who that was. But that's a good point to follow up on. Buddy, do you remember a whistling sound when you breathed at the game?
Kind of. Like a whistly sound when I breathe out. Not all the time.
Alright. Now, has he had any fever recently, or been sick with a cold?
No fever. He had a little sniffle a couple of weeks ago, but nothing since then.
And when he coughs, does he bring up any yellow or green phlegm?
No, nothing comes up. It's just a dry cough.
Good. Let's talk about his medicines. Can you tell me what he takes and how?
Sure. There's the fluticasone, that's the daily inhaler. He's supposed to take it twice a day, morning and night, with the spacer.
I take it every day. I never forget.
Buddy, I'm sorry, but he skips the morning one a lot. We're always rushing for the bus. Nights I make sure of.
I appreciate you both being honest. We'll come back to that. What else is he using?
The albuterol, for when he gets wheezy. He takes it when he needs it, and I'd say maybe twice a week. And the montelukast, 5 mg chewable, at bedtime.
Alright. Any other health problems, besides the asthma? I see eczema in his chart.
Yeah, he still gets dry patches in the elbow creases.
Okay. And any surgeries in the past?
His mom told me he had his tonsils out when he was five.
Good to know. Does anyone in the family have asthma, that you know of?
His dad has asthma too.
That fits the pattern, asthma often runs in families. Buddy, what do you like to do for fun, besides recess?
I play soccer on Saturdays. I'm a goalie, so I don't run that much.
Let me get his numbers now. Sit tight, buddy.
Temperature is 36.9 degrees Celsius, heart rate is 92 beats per minute, and breathing rate is 20 breaths per minute.
Oxygen saturation is 98 percent, and he weighs 72 pounds today.
Is that good, Doctor?
The numbers are all in a comfortable range, so nothing to worry about there. Now, how about his tummy and bowels, any problems there?
No, his stomach is fine.

Great. Let me explain what I think is going on. With the squeezy chest on running, the night cough several nights a week, and the wheeze at the game, it sounds like his asthma isn't fully controlled right now.
Is that because he misses the morning inhaler?
Very likely. The daily inhaler calms the lining of the airways, but only if it's used every day, like brushing teeth.
So I have to do it every morning?
Yes, and here's a trick: keep the inhaler right next to your toothbrush, and take your puffs before you brush. Then rinse your mouth.
That I can do. I'll put it right next to the toothbrush tonight.
Wonderful. And the albuterol, buddy: take it before soccer, every Saturday.
I'm not changing his medicines today, since I'd like to see first how he does when the daily inhaler is taken properly.
Let's see him again in six weeks, and we'll check how the cough and the squeezy chest are doing.
I'll book it at the front desk. And if he gets bad before then?
If he needs the albuterol more than usual, or he's struggling to breathe, call us right away or go to the emergency room.
Thank you so much, Doctor. Come on, let's get you a snack.

chief_complaint.normalized_value: Chest tightness on exertion; asthma review

symptoms.name: cough at night
symptoms.frequency: at least three nights a week

review_of_systems.details: No problems with stomach or bowels

clinical_actions.description: Take the daily controller inhaler every morning and night before brushing teeth and rinse mouth; use albuterol before soccer and carry it in the bag
Call or go to the emergency room if albuterol need increases or breathing is difficult

clinical_uncertainties.description: Fluticasone is prescribed twice a day; the patient says he takes it every day while the caregiver says he often skips the morning dose.
An unidentified voice from the hallway reported wheezing at a soccer game.
